items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1957-03-27
items.q: Mike Murray was very sensational. Very good drummer. ... Last time I heard him, he was playing on Rampart ... Last time I heard Mike Murray, last time I can recall him.

ctx.x: Old drummers, that is the first drummers that inspired you. People like Red Happy you were talking about.

Yeah, Red Happy. Just how they played? They had a lot of good drummers. Mike Murray was very sensational. Very good drummer. They had a tune that the band used to play. And they had a break. They used to make, you know, Mike Murray always carried a lot of contraptions with them, whistles and different kind of ratchets and all that for breaks, you know. And in this particular tune, he had a chain, you know, like they have on the wagons, a horse and wagon, a chain, a horse to the shaft. Well, they take this chain…

items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1959-12-23
items.q: Do you remember any particular tunes that Mike Murray would take breaks in? ... I had a set around that time

ctx.x: When did that come in? Oh, let's see.

Well, I can recall that came around 20, uh, 24, 25, I remember. I had a set around that time, yeah. I might have been a little before that, you know, but I mean, that's the time I had a set. That's about as far as I can remember having a set, you know. Do you remember any particular tunes that Mike Murray would take breaks in? No, I can't, uh, it's a tune that, uh, I can't recall his tune, uh, he had a, a wagon, a wagon chains. Uh-huh. And he'd hold them in the air and he'd, and he'd drop the chains to make a…
What has happened to cymbal playing, you know, the different changes in cymbal playing? I'd say, when you started out, what did they use a cymbal for? How would they use it and when?
